newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia says economic growth up 8.6 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia says economic growth up 8.6 pct in 96.

text.p: Saudi Arabia said on Monday its economy grew 8.6 percent in 1996 up from 4.3 in 1995 marking the third straight year of positive economic growth.
A Finance Ministry statement issued by the official media said gross domestic product (GDP) in 1996 reached 510 billion riyals ($136 billion) at current prices up from 469 billion riyals in 1995.
The private sector's contribution to GDP was 35 percent. The sector's growth stood at 3.5 percent in the year.

The statement said this showed the vitality of the private sector "not only in economic activity but in the increase in its contribution to the national economy" and was a sign of the success of government policies to diversify the oil-dependent economy. It said inflation in 1996 was expected to rise "by an average of less than one percent compared to the previous year."
The government had said that price rises in 1995 had led "for one time only" to a five percent increase in inflation.

The statement said the balance of payment registered "noticeable improvement" and added that the current account registered a surplus of 700 million riyals compared to a deficit of 19.9 billion riyals in 1995 "which was achieved mainly due to the improvement in the trade balance."
